title: Notification center
summary: Build inbox CRUD, preferences, delivery jobs, provider adapters, callbacks, and daily digests.
outcome: A notification service that respects user choices and makes delivery outcomes observable without pretending every timeout means failure.
prerequisites: Reliable sync, outbox transactions, request identity, and clock-based testing. Start with fake providers and generated recipient data.
model: Notification: id, recipientId, topic, payloadVersion, createdAt. InboxState: notificationId, readAt, archivedAt.
Preference: recipientId, topic, channel, enabled. Delivery: notificationId, channel, state, operationId, providerId, attempts.
DigestWindow groups eligible events for one recipient and interval. Separate user-visible inbox state from external delivery status.
boundaries: Accepted domain event → notification/outbox transaction → preference-aware worker → provider adapter → authenticated callback reducer.

milestones.title: Create a per-user notification inbox
milestones.brief: List, read, mark unread, and archive notifications while keeping each recipient's state isolated and stable across devices.
milestones.explanation: Notification content and a user's read state are different records with different lifetimes. Repeated mark-read commands should not create duplicate content or reset meaningful timestamps unexpectedly. Define what unread means after an archive or restore action, and apply the same rule to counts and filtered lists.
steps: Create fixtures for unread, read, archived, and missing notifications across two recipients. Specify state transitions and timestamp semantics.
Implement recipient-scoped reads and idempotent state commands with loading, empty, and failed-action UI states.
Test repeated updates, a notification disappearing while open, and simultaneous changes from two clients. Compare counts with the actual filtered records.

checks.label: Recipients cannot read or change another user's inbox state.
Repeated commands preserve the declared timestamp semantics.
Unread counts agree with list and archive behavior.

milestones.experiment: Mark a notification read in one tab while archiving it in another. Verify the resulting state follows a defined rule rather than whichever UI response arrived last.
milestones.review: Ask the agent to identify the authoritative state and explain whether updates commute. Keep delivery status out of the user's read/unread model.
milestones.stretch: Add bulk mark-read with an explicit cutoff so newly arriving notifications are not silently included.

milestones.title: Respect channel and topic preferences
milestones.brief: Let users manage notification preferences and enforce those choices when delivery occurs, including queued work.
milestones.explanation: A preference captured when an event was created may be stale when a worker sends it. Define which policy is evaluated at creation and which at delivery. Distinguish optional product topics from any separately defined essential messages, and never let a client-supplied category bypass the server's topic policy.
steps: Write a topic/channel matrix with defaults, supported overrides, and treatment of missing preference records.
Implement validated preference CRUD and a delivery eligibility service. Show the effect of a change using representative pending notifications.
Queue a notification, disable its channel, then run delivery. Test restored preferences, unknown topics, and direct unauthorized updates.

checks.label: Preferences affect delivery according to the documented timing rule.
Unsupported topics and channels are rejected consistently.
A user can modify only their own preference records.

milestones.experiment: Pause a worker immediately before provider submission and change the preference. State the decision boundary and verify behavior at that boundary.
milestones.review: A checkbox label should explain the actual policy. Avoid implying immediate cancellation of a provider request that has already been accepted.
milestones.stretch: Version topic definitions and test how new topics inherit defaults for existing users.

milestones.title: Queue notifications atomically
milestones.brief: Create notification intent with the originating business event and expand recipients without unbounded synchronous work.
milestones.explanation: If a business update commits and notification intent is lost, a retrying worker cannot recover what was never recorded. Put durable intent in the same transaction where possible. Large fan-out needs bounded batches and a checkpoint, and recipient identity must be part of the duplicate-prevention key.
steps: Choose one originating event, such as a ticket assignment. Define its stable identity, recipient resolution, and duplicate policy.
Commit event and outbox intent together, then expand recipients in bounded batches with durable progress.
Inject failure before intent commit, during recipient expansion, and after a batch completes but before acknowledgement. Compare recipient delivery identities.

checks.label: Committed events retain their required notification intent.
Restarted expansion does not duplicate recipient notifications.
Batch size and active work remain within documented limits.

milestones.experiment: Restart fan-out after the first half of recipients have been inserted. Verify the completed half is recognized instead of recreated.
milestones.review: Separate at-least-once processing from user-visible duplicates. Explain the unique keys and transaction boundaries that connect those two concerns.
milestones.stretch: Add per-workspace fairness so a large audience cannot starve small interactive notifications.

milestones.title: Swap providers and classify failures
milestones.brief: Implement fake and live-shaped provider adapters with a common contract for accepted, rejected, rate-limited, and ambiguous responses.
milestones.explanation: Provider APIs differ in error meaning and idempotency support. Normalize their responses at the adapter boundary without erasing distinctions the delivery policy needs. A timeout after submission may mean unknown outcome. Retries need a finite budget, and failover can duplicate a message if the first provider actually accepted it.
steps: Define an adapter interface and fixtures for acceptance, permanent rejection, rate limiting, timeout, and malformed responses.
Implement a deterministic fake Layer and provider-shaped adapter. Map failures into explicit categories and cap retry time and attempts.
Test a lost accepted response, repeated rate limits, and a permanent address failure. Record operation IDs and provider receipts without logging message secrets.

checks.label: All adapter outcomes map to documented delivery states.
Permanent failures do not enter blind retry loops.
Ambiguous outcomes are represented honestly and remain diagnosable.

milestones.experiment: Accept a message in the fake provider but drop its response. Try a fallback provider and explain the duplicate risk before choosing a policy.
milestones.review: Do not infer delivery to a human from provider acceptance. Keep submitted, accepted, delivered, and read meanings distinct.
milestones.stretch: Add a provider circuit policy and verify that recovery probes do not release an unbounded retry surge.

milestones.title: Process delivery callbacks safely
milestones.brief: Update delivery state from verified provider callbacks that may arrive twice, late, or in an unexpected order.
milestones.explanation: Callbacks are untrusted network input until their authenticity and schema are checked. Keep the provider's event identity and relate it to a known delivery. Define which state transitions are allowed so a late accepted event cannot overwrite a later delivered or failed state without an explicit rule.
steps: Create callback fixtures for delivered, bounced, duplicate, unknown receipt, invalid signature, and out-of-order events.
Verify callbacks using the provider's documented raw-body/signature contract, then store a receipt and apply the transition atomically.
Replay callbacks in different orders and restart after receipt insertion failure. Keep invalid events from mutating delivery records.

checks.label: Unverified callbacks cannot alter delivery state.
Duplicate events are acknowledged without duplicate transitions.
Out-of-order events follow the declared state model.

milestones.experiment: Deliver a final outcome followed by an older intermediate event. Verify the later arrival does not regress the meaningful state.
milestones.review: Explain the difference between transport arrival time and provider event time. Preserve enough provenance to investigate contradictory callbacks.
milestones.stretch: Add a quarantined view for unknown provider receipts and a reviewed reconciliation procedure.

milestones.title: Build resumable daily digests
milestones.concept: Windowed jobs · clock and checkpoint services
milestones.brief: Group eligible notifications into a daily digest with explicit time-zone windows and recovery after interrupted processing.
milestones.explanation: A daily digest is a windowing policy, not merely a cron expression. Define which event timestamps qualify, how late events are handled, and which recipient zone sets the day boundary. Persist a window identity and checkpoint so rerunning a job does not resend the same digest or skip unprocessed recipients.
steps: Specify digest windows, late-arrival policy, recipient preferences, and empty-window behavior. Include a daylight-saving boundary fixture.
Build bounded recipient processing with a unique digest identity and provider adapter. Persist composition before delivery so retries use the same content.
Interrupt processing mid-window, resume, then rerun the entire job. Compare window receipts, recipient counts, and final inbox content.

checks.label: Events belong to the documented window, including boundary cases.
Restart and rerun do not create duplicate digest identities.
Preferences and empty-window behavior remain consistent.

milestones.experiment: Insert an event for yesterday after yesterday's digest has been composed. Verify it follows the declared late-arrival policy instead of disappearing silently.
milestones.review: Use a fake clock and inspect persisted window boundaries. Record whether external delivery can still be ambiguous despite local duplicate prevention.
milestones.stretch: Add a dry-run digest preview and a recovery report for recipients left unprocessed after a provider outage.
